title: Avo-6-Part-5
description: Exam covering TCAS, GPWS, EGPWS, FMS, FMC, CDU, IMA, OIS, on-board maintenance systems, and aircraft warning systems. Options and explanations are grounded in the ET-AV06 M5: Typical Avionics System (Level 2) reference note, with each question reduced to three answer choices while preserving the originally supplied correct answer.

questions.question: According to ICAO Annex 6, which aircraft must be equipped with a ground proximity warning system that has a forward-looking terrain avoidance function?
options: A. All turbine-engine airplanes with a maximum take-off mass over 15,000 kg, or authorized to carry more than 30 passengers
B. Only piston-engine airplanes below 5,700 kg
C. Only helicopters used for commercial operations
questions.explanation: ICAO Annex 6, Chapter 6 states that all turbine-engine airplanes of a maximum certificated take-off mass in excess of 15,000 kg, or authorized to carry more than 30 passengers, must be equipped with a GPWS having a forward-looking terrain avoidance function.

questions.question: According to ICAO Annex 10, which of the following is a required function of ACAS II (TCAS II)?
options: B. Detection of collision threats and generation of resolution advisories to avoid them
questions.explanation: ICAO Annex 10 lists the required ACAS II functions as surveillance and generation of traffic advisories, detection of collision threats and generation of resolution advisories to avoid them, coordination with other suitably equipped aircraft, and communication with ground stations.

questions.question: Which aural warning is given for a steep, excessive descent rate close to the ground?
questions.explanation: GPWS Mode 1 covers a large descent rate. If the descent rate continues or increases, the alert changes to a warning with the PULL-UP light and the aural message "WHOOP WHOOP PULL-UP."

questions.question: What shape represents a Resolution Advisory (RA) on the TCAS/EFIS display?
questions.explanation: The reference explains that once an intruder is assessed as an actual collision threat the TCAS display symbol changes to a solid red square (a filled red box on the EFIS), together with a voice Resolution Advisory command.

questions.question: What is TCAS I intended to provide?
options: A. Proximity warning only, to assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of an intruder aircraft
B. Resolution advisories with vertical maneuver guidance
C. A ground-proximity warning against terrain
questions.explanation: TCAS I provides proximity warning only to assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of intruder aircraft, and it is intended for smaller commuter and general aviation aircraft.

questions.question: On an aircraft such as the A380, which unit is used by cabin crew for cabin operations and to access their electronic documentation?
options: B. Flight Attendant Panel (FAP) / cabin access panel
questions.explanation: The reference describes the Flight Attendant Panels (FAPs) as touchscreen units used by the cabin crew to access cabin applications and electronic documentation for cabin operations.

questions.question: The basic principle of TCAS operation is most closely related to which surveillance technique?
options: A. Displaying only weather radar returns
B. Secondary surveillance radar (interrogating transponders on SSR frequencies)
C. Detecting and tracking nearby aircraft using an onboard terrain database
questions.explanation: TCAS/ACAS detects nearby intruder aircraft by interrogating their transponders, which reply to Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS) Mode C or Mode S interrogations on SSR frequencies (1030/1090 MHz) — the same principle used by secondary surveillance radar.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the required inputs to TCAS II?
options: A. Own aircraft's maximum cruising true airspeed capability
B. Pressure altitude and radio altitude
questions.explanation: TCAS II requires the aircraft address code, air-to-air Mode S transmissions, own aircraft's maximum cruising true airspeed, pressure altitude, and radio altitude. A terrain/airport database is not a TCAS input — it belongs to the (E)GPWS.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the typical aural warning events listed for the flight compartment aural warning system?
options: C. Unsafe take-off or landing configuration
questions.explanation: The reference lists abnormal take-off/landing, cabin pressurization, overspeed/Mach conditions, engine or wheel-well fire, crew-call and collision-avoidance recommendations as events triggering aural warnings; a cabin temperature alert is not among these discrete aural-warning inputs.

questions.question: In the A350 Flight Warning System alert classification, which level does NOT have an associated aural warning?
questions.explanation: Level 0 indications cover operational or system conditions for which only a flight-deck indication (such as a memo or ECAM advisory) is required, so they do not carry an aural warning, unlike Level 2 and Level 3 alerts.

questions.question: Where is the stall warning test typically carried out and monitored from?
options: A. The cockpit, using the stall warning test/control panel
questions.explanation: The reference's B737-200 stall warning test description is centred on the cockpit stall warning panel, where the test is initiated and its indications are observed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function controlled by the TCAS computer?
options: B. Communication with ATC ground stations
questions.explanation: The reference states that the TCAS computer controls surveillance, tracking, advisory, and air-to-air maneuver coordination. Direct communication with ground stations is not one of the functions the TCAS computer itself performs.

questions.question: How is Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) more scalable than a traditional (federated) architecture?
options: A. By sharing common computing and communication resources across different applications
B. By installing a separate dedicated processor for every application
C. By increasing the number of LRUs and the amount of point-to-point wiring
questions.explanation: IMA replaces numerous separate processors and LRUs with fewer, centralized processing modules that host multiple software applications on shared computing and communication resources, making the architecture easier to expand than the traditional one-LRU-per-function approach.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical cause that would trigger a GPWS alert?
options: A. A high descent rate at low altitude
B. Normal cruise flight at a constant altitude
C. A high cabin temperature reading
questions.explanation: The hazardous conditions listed for GPWS include excessive descent rate, excessive bank angle at low altitude, insufficient terrain clearance, and excessive closure rate to terrain — a high descent rate at low altitude is a classic trigger.

questions.question: Which classification of traffic causes TCAS to issue a Resolution Advisory (RA)?
options: C. Information from the navigation database
questions.explanation: The reference defines threat traffic as airplanes with an altitude separation of about ±900 feet and a time to closest point of approach of less than 25 seconds — this class of traffic is what causes the TCAS computer to generate a Resolution Advisory.

questions.question: Which OIS domain is primarily used to provide services to passengers?
questions.explanation: The Onboard Information System applications are hosted on three domains — avionics, flight operations, and communication and cabin. The communication and cabin domain is the one associated with cabin/passenger-facing services.

questions.question: What initiates a TCAS II Resolution Advisory (RA)?
options: A. A predicted violation of the safe vertical separation boundary as the intruder continues to close
B. Low fuel quantity on board
C. An excessive cabin temperature reading
questions.explanation: TCAS II predicts the time to, and separation at, the intruder's closest point of approach. If the intruder continues to close and safe boundaries would be violated, TCAS II issues a Resolution Advisory to maintain safe vertical separation.

questions.question: How much fuel/energy can performance management typically save through optimized flight performance?
options: A. Fuel flow is increased during cruise for a safety margin
B. About 1 to 2% of energy can be saved through the best flight strategy
C. The navigation database is disabled to reduce processing load
questions.explanation: The reference states that through selection of the best strategy in FMS performance management, between 1 and 2% of energy can be saved.

questions.question: Why is EGPWS considered an improvement over the original GPWS?
options: A. It relies solely on the radio altimeter for all alerting decisions
B. It contains a worldwide terrain and airport database compared with aircraft position and track
C. It can operate fully without knowing the aircraft's position
questions.explanation: The EGPWS contains a worldwide terrain and airport database and compares the airplane's position and track against this database, incorporating terrain alerting and display functions that the basic GPWS does not have.

questions.question: How does the FMCS enhance performance by checking the vertical and horizontal flight profile?
options: A. By calculating a flight path that gives the shortest flying time at the lowest fuel consumption
B. By continuously displaying cabin temperature to the crew
C. By generating TCAS resolution advisories
questions.explanation: The FMS/FMC contains a performance database and calculates a vertical profile (combined with the lateral/horizontal path) that gives the shortest possible flying time at the lowest fuel consumption, which is how it enhances overall flight performance.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of IMA compared with a conventional federated avionics architecture?
options: A. It requires more LRUs than a conventional architecture
B. It requires a dedicated processor for every function
C. It requires fewer LRUs by sharing centralized processing resources
questions.explanation: IMA replaces numerous separate processors and LRUs with fewer, more centralized processing units, reducing the LRU count compared with the conventional federated approach.

questions.question: On a typical maintenance panel, what indicates that a fault has been recorded by the maintenance system?
questions.explanation: The maintenance panel's Bite Loaded Indicator specifically indicates when a fault has been recorded by the maintenance system.

questions.question: For two aircraft to obtain fully coordinated air-to-air TCAS maneuvers, what equipment is required on both the host aircraft and the intruder?
options: A. Both aircraft must carry TCAS II equipment capable of coordinated resolution advisories
B. Only a VHF communication radio is required on both aircraft
C. Only weather radar is required on both aircraft
questions.explanation: The levels-of-protection table shows that TCAS-TCAS coordination (TTC), where advisories are coordinated between the two aircraft via a Mode S data link, is only available when both aircraft carry TCAS II (or better) equipment.

questions.question: Which of the following describes an advantage of IMA?
options: A. More wiring and more separate boxes than a conventional architecture
B. A dedicated prognostic Aircraft Vibration Monitoring function
C. Both weight saving (less wiring and boxes) and cost reduction
questions.explanation: The reference lists the advantages of IMA's shared, centralized computing approach as weight saving through less wiring and fewer boxes, together with cost reduction.

questions.question: What is the crew's main interface with the Flight Management Computer (FMC)?
options: A. The Control and Display Unit (CDU)
C. The weather radar control panel
questions.explanation: The CDU is the means of communication with the FMC: it lets the crew input flight and performance details before flight and displays the navigation and performance computations for reference.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the FMC?
options: A. Flight planning and performance calculations
B. Detecting the presence of a nearby intruder aircraft
C. Providing flight guidance and control commands
questions.explanation: The FMC is described as the heart of the FMS, performing navigational and performance calculations and providing control and guidance commands; detecting a nearby intruder aircraft is a TCAS function, not an FMC one.

questions.question: What does a solid red terrain color indicate on an EGPWS terrain display?
questions.explanation: Table 5.1 of the reference lists solid red as indicating a terrain/obstacle threat warning on the EGPWS display.

questions.question: Which system is a set of electronic documentation and applications for flight, maintenance, and cabin operations, replacing paper documentation?
questions.explanation: The reference defines the Onboard Information System (OIS) as a set of electronic documentation and applications for flight, maintenance, and cabin operations that replaces previously used paper documentation.

questions.question: Which panel do cabin crew use for cabin operations, such as consulting cabin documentation and forms?
questions.explanation: The Flight Attendant Panels (FAPs) are described as touchscreens used by the cabin crew to access their electronic documentation and forms for cabin operations.

questions.question: Which unit does the pilot use to load flight and performance data into the FMC before flight?
questions.explanation: The CDU is used before flight to initialize the performance and navigation requirements, allowing the crew to input flight details and performance parameters into the FMC.

questions.question: Which component is the heart of the FMS, performing all navigational and performance calculations and providing control and guidance commands?
questions.explanation: The reference states that the Flight Management Computer (FMC) is the heart of the system, performing all the navigational and performance calculations and providing control and guidance commands.

questions.question: An excessive descent rate is detected under which GPWS mode?
questions.explanation: GPWS Mode 1 covers a large descent rate: it warns the pilot when the aircraft is below about 2,450 feet radio altitude with an excessive rate of descent, triggering "SINK RATE" or "WHOOP WHOOP PULL-UP."

questions.question: The TCAS airborne equipment consists of an interrogator, transmitter, and receiver operating on which SSR frequencies?
questions.explanation: TCAS airborne equipment consists of an interrogator, transmitter, and receiver operating on SSR frequencies of 1030 MHz and 1090 MHz respectively.

questions.question: Which component of the FMS allows the crew to input flight details and performance parameters into the FMC?
questions.explanation: The CDU allows the crew to input the flight details and performance parameters into the FMC, and it displays the navigation and performance computations for reference and monitoring.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of IMA?
options: A. More wiring and more separate boxes
C. Fewer LRUs than a conventional architecture
questions.explanation: IMA is intended to reduce wiring and the number of boxes by sharing centralized computing resources across applications, so "more wiring and boxes" describes the conventional architecture, not an IMA advantage.

questions.question: Where is the CDU normally located?
options: C. In the main landing gear bay
questions.explanation: The CDU is the crew's interface with the FMC and is located in the cockpit, where the flight crew uses it before and during flight.

questions.question: Which system provides traffic advisories and resolution advisories in the vertical direction to avoid conflicting traffic?
questions.explanation: TCAS II provides traffic advisories and resolution advisories (recommended escape maneuvers) in the vertical direction to avoid conflicting traffic, and is used on airline, larger commuter, and business aircraft.

questions.question: Which warning sound is heard in the cockpit when airspeed or Mach number exceeds structural limits?
options: B. A TCAS resolution advisory tone
questions.explanation: The B737 aural warning module list includes overspeed clackers among the sounds produced in the flight compartment, used to alert the crew when airspeed/Mach limits are exceeded.

questions.question: Which two colors are typically used for warning and caution lights?
questions.explanation: The reference states that red warning lights show conditions requiring immediate corrective action, while amber (yellow) caution lights show conditions that do not immediately affect flight capability.

questions.question: White and blue (or green) color indications in the cockpit generally represent what?
options: A. A condition requiring immediate crew action
B. A caution requiring future corrective action
C. Advisory information / normal system operation
questions.explanation: The reference explains that green lights show safe system operation and white or blue lights show normal operation — these represent advisory or normal-status information rather than a caution or warning.

questions.question: Which function supplies trend and servicing monitoring reports for the detection, in advance, of a possible failure appearance?
questions.explanation: The Onboard Maintenance System's prognostic function operates on aircraft operational data and supplies trend and servicing monitoring reports for the detection in advance of a possible failure appearance.

questions.question: Which TCAS component controls surveillance, tracking, advisory generation, and air-to-air maneuver coordination?
questions.explanation: The TCAS computer is the main TCAS component, controlling surveillance, tracking, advisory generation, and air-to-air maneuver coordination.

questions.question: The FMC computes the flight plan and shows it on which display?
questions.explanation: The FMS also gives information to the EFIS to show the flight plan on the Navigation Display (ND), so the crew can monitor the aircraft's progress relative to the plan.

questions.question: What does IMA use to replace numerous separate processors and LRUs?
options: C. Fewer, more centralized processing units
questions.explanation: The Integrated Modular Avionics concept replaces numerous separate processors and line-replaceable units with fewer, more centralized processing units.

questions.question: What is the term used for the onboard maintenance computer that processes fault information and supplies maintenance messages?
questions.explanation: The Central Maintenance Computer System (CMCS) monitors the airplane's systems for faults, processes fault information, supplies maintenance messages, and monitors flight-deck effects.

questions.question: The objective of which system is to ensure timely crew action is taken during a terrain-related alert or warning?
questions.explanation: The GPWS is designed to alert the flight crew to an unsafe condition due to terrain proximity so that timely corrective action can be taken, using both visual and aural annunciations.

questions.question: Below approximately what radio altitude does GPWS Mode 1 (large descent rate) alerting become active?
questions.explanation: The reference states that GPWS Mode 1 warnings occur when the aircraft is below approximately 2,450 feet radio altitude with an excessive rate of descent, with alerts/warnings possible between about 30 and 2,450 feet.

questions.question: Which warning sound is heard in the cockpit for an engine fire?
questions.explanation: The aural warning module produces fire bells among its outputs, and a bell also sounds for related unsafe conditions such as retarding the throttle with the gear not down and locked.

questions.question: On the TCAS navigation display, which symbol indicates that the intruder aircraft is above your own altitude?
options: A. A minus sign with a number below the symbol
B. A plus sign with a number above the symbol
C. A zero with no sign
questions.explanation: A + sign and number displayed above the traffic symbol indicates the intruder is above your own altitude, while a – sign and number below indicates it is below.

questions.question: How many independent Flight Management Systems (FMS) does a typical commercial aircraft carry?
questions.explanation: A typical commercial aircraft carries two independent FMS/FMC installations for redundancy in navigation and performance computation.

questions.question: A TCAS traffic symbol appears on the display when other traffic is beyond which separation from your aircraft?
options: A. Proximate traffic only, regardless of distance
B. Within 2 nautical miles and 500 feet
C. More than 6 nautical miles, or more than 1,200 feet vertically
questions.explanation: A Traffic Advisory symbol that is not yet a threat initially appears as an open diamond, meaning the other traffic is more than 6 nautical miles away or more than 1,200 feet vertically from your aircraft.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically an input to the Ground Proximity Warning Computer (GPWC)?
options: B. Landing gear and flap position
questions.explanation: Typical GPWS inputs include the radio altimeter, air data computer, FMC, IRS, landing gear position, flap position, and VHF navigation receiver — a VHF voice communication transceiver is not among the listed GPWC inputs.

questions.question: On a typical ATR 72 maintenance panel, what does the BITE Advisory Display indicate?
options: A. It illuminates lights that record the code of the failure detected
B. It provides flight guidance commands to the autopilot
C. It displays the navigation database contents
questions.explanation: The Bite Advisory Display indicates, through illuminated lights, the code of the failure recorded, with combinations of lights able to code up to 14 failures per system.

questions.question: What does the GPWS/EGPWS self-test (BITE) capability perform?
options: A. A navigation display calibration test
B. A structured, multi-level periodic self-test of system functions
C. A cabin communication system test
questions.explanation: The EGPWS Self-Test capability consists of several levels (from a GO/NO-GO pre-flight check through current faults, configuration, fault history, warning history, and discrete test) used to verify and indicate intended functions.

questions.question: A Resolution Advisory (RA) typically occurs about how many seconds before the closest point of approach?
questions.explanation: The reference classifies threat traffic (which causes a Resolution Advisory) as having a time to closest point of approach of less than 25 seconds.

questions.question: Which TCAS advisory suggests a vertical maneuver to achieve safe separation and avoid a collision?
questions.explanation: The Resolution Advisory (RA) is the TCAS advisory that recommends an escape/vertical maneuver to maintain safe separation from the intruder and avoid a collision.

questions.question: In the A350 Flight Warning System, which alert level describes an abnormal aircraft situation requiring crew awareness and corrective action, without being an immediate emergency?
questions.explanation: A Level 2 alert refers to an abnormal situation of the aircraft for which crew awareness and subsequent corrective or compensatory action are necessary, as distinct from the immediate-reaction Level 3 emergency alerts.

questions.question: In the Onboard Maintenance System (OMS), the function of uploading/downloading software and files falls under which category?
questions.explanation: The OMS maintenance support functions specifically include software uploading and file downloading, alongside access to electronic maintenance documentation and interactive tests.

questions.question: For a fully coordinated maneuver between two aircraft using TCAS-TCAS coordination at the highest protection level, what equipment is required on both aircraft?
options: A. Both aircraft equipped for coordinated maneuvers (e.g., matching TCAS II/III capability)
B. A ground-proximity warning system only
questions.explanation: The levels-of-protection table shows that TCAS-TCAS coordination, which enables fully coordinated escape maneuvers, requires both the host and intruder aircraft to carry an appropriately equipped TCAS system.

questions.question: Which system performs all the calculations and predictions needed to determine the most economical flight profile?
questions.explanation: The FMC's performance database and calculations determine the vertical profile that gives the shortest flying time at the lowest fuel consumption — i.e., the most economical flight profile.

questions.question: How often is the aircraft's navigation database typically updated?
questions.explanation: The reference states that the navigation database is updated every 28 days, coinciding with the ICAO navigation data cycle, with the FMC holding the current and next 28-day database.

questions.question: Which avionics architecture uses a separate LRU for each dedicated system function, interconnected point-to-point?
questions.explanation: The conventional (federated) avionics approach uses a separate LRU for each avionics function, interconnected point-to-point using buses such as ARINC 429/629, which IMA was designed to replace with shared, centralized processing.

questions.question: To calculate the closest point of approach (CPA) and relative altitude of traffic, what does the TCAS computer primarily use?
options: A. The time until the CPA, together with own and traffic aircraft range, altitude, and airspeed
questions.explanation: To calculate the CPA and relative altitude, the TCAS computer uses the time until the CPA together with the TCAS airplane's airspeed and altitude, and the range, altitude, and airspeed of the traffic airplane.

questions.question: What is calculated when the FMS works out the vertical flight plan, optimizing speed and altitude?
options: A. The vertical and horizontal profile, based on aircraft weight, fuel weight, and time
B. Only the cabin service schedule
C. Only the maintenance fault history
questions.explanation: The FMS vertical flight plan calculation optimizes speed and altitude depending on aircraft weight, fuel weight, and time, together with aircraft/engine performance databases.

questions.question: Which computers can monitor and control several aircraft systems through multiple software applications hosted on shared resources?
questions.explanation: IMA computers can monitor and control several systems via several applications hosted on shared computing and communication resources, unlike the dedicated, single-function LRUs of a conventional architecture.

questions.question: During a Resolution Advisory (RA), where is a maneuver indication shown to guide the flight crew in avoiding a possible collision?
options: A. On the Primary Flight Displays (PFDs)
B. On the cabin service panel
C. On the fuel quantity indicator
questions.explanation: When a Resolution Advisory is generated, maneuver indications appear on the PFDs to guide the flight crew, in addition to indications on the NDs and aural annunciations from the warning speakers.

questions.question: GPWS bank-angle call-outs are provided as part of which mode?
questions.explanation: GPWS Mode 6 provides alerts and call-outs for descent below predefined altitudes and can also incorporate bank-angle protection call-outs.

questions.question: Which TCAS type will provide traffic advisories and resolution advisories in both the horizontal and vertical directions?
questions.explanation: TCAS III, still under development at the time of writing, is intended to provide traffic advisories and resolution advisories in the horizontal as well as the vertical direction, unlike TCAS II which is vertical-only.

questions.question: The FMS provides information to the EFIS to show the flight plan on which display?
options: A. The Primary Flight Display (PFD) only
questions.explanation: The FMS gives information to the EFIS to show the selected flight plan on the Navigation Display (ND), while flight path guidance is separately shown on the PFD.

questions.question: A GPWS terrain warning alert (as opposed to a caution) requires what kind of crew response?
questions.explanation: GPWS/EGPWS caution and warning envelopes are structured so that a warning-level terrain alert demands an immediate crew action, while a caution provides earlier notice for monitoring.

questions.question: Which GPWS mode alerts the crew to too much deviation below the ILS glideslope?
questions.explanation: GPWS Mode 5 covers too much deviation below the glideslope centerline; if the aircraft sinks below the glideslope, the amber GS light illuminates and the aural warning repeats "GLIDE SLOPE GLIDE SLOPE."

questions.question: EGPWS eliminates the "blind spots" of the original GPWS by comparing aircraft position (from GPS) against what?
options: A. A worldwide terrain and airport database
B. A cabin service schedule database
questions.explanation: The EGPWS eliminates the reactive-only limitation of basic GPWS by comparing the airplane's GPS-derived position and track against a worldwide terrain and airport database to predict conflicts ahead of the aircraft.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a system component/interface of the GPWS?
questions.explanation: GPWS interfaces listed in the reference include the radio altimeter, air data computer, inertial reference unit, stall warning system, landing gear handle, flap/stab position module, and ILS receiver — a TCAS antenna is not one of them.

questions.question: How are TCAS interrogations and replies exchanged between two TCAS-equipped aircraft for coordinated maneuvers?
options: A. Directly between the onboard Mode S transponders, using a data link
B. Through the cabin interphone system
C. Through the weather radar transmitter
questions.explanation: Two TCAS II-equipped aircraft coordinate their resolution advisories directly, using a Mode S transponder data link between the onboard equipment, without needing ATC or ground station relay.

questions.question: Navigation facility details such as location, altitude, frequency, and identification of ILS/VOR/DME stations are examples of what?
options: A. Contents of the navigation database
B. Contents of the cabin service database
C. Contents of the maintenance fault log
questions.explanation: The navigation database contains aerodrome details and navigation facilities (ILS, VOR, DME), including their location, altitude, frequency, and identification, along with airways, SIDs, STARs, and company routes.

questions.question: On which display is flight path guidance information shown to the pilot?
options: C. A multi-function engine display only
questions.explanation: Flight path guidance and steering commands generated by the FMS/AFS are shown to the crew primarily on the Primary Flight Display (PFD), via the flight director command cues.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Flight Management System (FMS)?
options: A. Calculating the lateral and vertical flight plan
B. Managing performance predictions such as fuel and arrival time
C. Automatically switching between different types of radio communications
questions.explanation: The FMS's role is centered on navigation, guidance, and performance management (flight plan, fuel and time predictions); automatically switching between different communication systems is not one of its listed functions.

questions.question: Which of the following describes a general function of Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA)?
options: A. To supply a centralized computing and data communication capability
B. To operate only the flight attendant call system
C. To control only hydraulic system pressure
questions.explanation: The reference states that the general function of IMA is to organize shared resources and to supply a centralized computing and data communication capability for multiple aircraft systems.

questions.question: Which system lets the crew access the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) and Configuration Deviation List (CDL) electronically?
options: C. The Onboard Information System (OIS), via its avionics domain electronic documentation
questions.explanation: The OIS avionics domain hosts electronic documentation needed by flight and maintenance crew, including the MEL and CDL, giving electronic access instead of using paper manuals.

questions.question: An amber caution light typically shows what kind of condition?
options: A. A green, fully normal operating condition
B. A system malfunction or condition that does not immediately affect the aircraft's flight capability
questions.explanation: The reference explains that amber caution lights show system malfunctions or conditions that do not immediately affect the aircraft's flight capabilities but that possibly require future corrective action.

questions.question: Where is the Flight Management Computer (FMC) typically installed on the aircraft?
options: A. In the main equipment center
B. On the cockpit overhead panel
C. In the main landing gear bay
questions.explanation: Like most large avionics LRUs, the FMC is typically installed in the aircraft's main equipment center, with the CDU as its remote cockpit interface.

questions.question: How many channels does a typical aircraft aural warning unit (e.g., on the ATR 72 / B737-type systems) have?
questions.explanation: The reference states that the aural warning module has two channels, connected in parallel, with a 6 dB reduction in audio output if one channel fails.

questions.question: GPWS Mode 1 terrain-awareness cautions/warnings are given for what condition?
questions.explanation: GPWS Mode 1 is specifically the large-descent-rate mode: it triggers "SINK RATE" and, if the condition worsens, "WHOOP WHOOP PULL-UP."

questions.question: During the pre-flight phase, what does the FMS calculate for the aircraft based on the entered weight and cruise altitude?
options: A. The vertical and horizontal (lateral) flight profile
B. Only the cabin temperature profile
C. Only the maintenance fault profile
questions.explanation: Once the lateral flight plan is selected, additional data such as weight and cruise altitude is inserted so the FMS can calculate the vertical flight plan together with the lateral flight plan, forming the overall flight profile.

questions.question: In the A350 Flight Warning System, which alert level refers to an emergency situation requiring the crew's immediate reaction?
questions.explanation: A Level 3 alert refers to an emergency situation, such as ENGINE/APU FIRE or OVERSPEED, for which an immediate reaction of the crew is necessary — the highest urgency in the FWS classification.

questions.question: What is the purpose of TCAS Traffic Advisories (TAs)?
options: A. To assist the crew in visually searching for and identifying an intruder aircraft
B. To automatically generate a terrain database
C. To directly control the flight management computer's flight plan
questions.explanation: A Traffic Advisory alerts the crew that closing traffic is in the vicinity, helping them visually search for and identify the intruder aircraft before any escape maneuver is required.

questions.question: Red warning lights typically indicate what type of condition?
options: A. Conditions requiring an amber-level future action only
B. Fully normal, green-level system operation
C. System malfunctions or conditions that cause dangerous flight conditions, requiring immediate action
questions.explanation: The reference states that red warning lights show system malfunctions or conditions that cause dangerous flight conditions and require an immediate corrective action.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid purpose of structural (health) monitoring as applied to aircraft engines?
options: A. Detecting failures only after real damage has already occurred
B. Preventing engine damage and possible hazard following a catastrophic failure
C. Detecting changes in engine speed, temperature, pressure, and vibration before damage occurs
questions.explanation: Structural/health monitoring was first applied to engines specifically to prevent damage and to detect failures before any real damage occurs — detecting them only after the damage has already happened defeats this purpose.

questions.question: On a typical ATR 72 maintenance panel, how are recorded faults indicated to the technician?
options: A. Through two independent aural-warning channels
B. By detecting the presence of a nearby intruder aircraft
C. By illuminating lights and recording the failure code on the Bite Advisory Display
questions.explanation: The maintenance panel indicates recorded faults by illuminating lights and recording the failure code on the Bite Advisory Display, using combinations of lights to code up to 14 failures per system.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT true with respect to the Integrated Modular Avionics architecture?
options: A. It supports a prognostic health-monitoring capability
B. It always increases the overall lifecycle/maintenance cost of the avionics suite
C. It relies on shared resources and centralized processing
questions.explanation: IMA is intended to reduce, not increase, lifecycle and maintenance costs by sharing centralized processing resources across applications, so a claim that it always increases lifecycle cost is not consistent with its design goals.

questions.question: Which TCAS type is intended for use by smaller commuter and general aviation aircraft?
questions.explanation: TCAS I provides proximity warning only, to assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of intruder aircraft, and is intended for use by smaller commuter and general aviation aircraft.

questions.question: What is the general function of Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA)?
options: A. To supply a centralized computing and data communication capability
B. To provide terrain warning only
C. To provide secondary surveillance radar only
questions.explanation: The reference describes the general function of IMA as organizing shared resources and supplying a centralized computing and data communication capability across multiple applications.

questions.question: A TCAS traffic symbol first appears on the display when other traffic is beyond what separation from the aircraft?
options: A. More than 6 nautical miles or more than 1,200 feet vertically
B. Any distance defined only by the navigation database
C. Any distance defined only by the cabin domain
questions.explanation: Other traffic that is more than 6 nautical miles away or more than 1,200 feet vertically from your aircraft is initially shown as an open (non-threat) diamond symbol on the display.

questions.question: Which system is the heart of the aircraft, performing all navigational and performance calculations and providing control and guidance commands?
options: A. The terrain/obstacle threat warning system
B. The Flight Management Computer System (FMCS)
C. A cabin warning indication panel
questions.explanation: The Flight Management Computer System (FMCS) is described as the heart of the system, performing all navigational and performance calculations and providing control and guidance commands.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a TCAS Traffic Advisory (TA)?
options: A. To command an immediate corrective vertical maneuver
B. To assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of the intruder aircraft
C. To automatically update the navigation database
questions.explanation: A Traffic Advisory is intended to assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of the intruder aircraft and to alert the crew that closing traffic is nearby, ahead of any resolution advisory.

questions.question: How many independent FMS installations does a typical commercial aircraft carry?
questions.explanation: A typical commercial aircraft carries two independent FMS/FMC installations for redundancy.

questions.question: Which database contains the aeronautical information for the planned area of operations of the aircraft?
options: A. Own aircraft's GPS position log
C. The list of onboard FMS computers
questions.explanation: The navigation database contains aeronautical information for the planned area of operations of the aircraft, including aerodrome details, navigation facilities, airways, SIDs, STARs, and company routes.

questions.question: Which type of information does the Central Maintenance Computer (CMC) NOT typically provide?
options: A. Fault and maintenance-related information from aircraft systems, including TCAS BITE data
B. Flight operations information (such as performance or navigation planning tools)
C. Guidance commands from the FMS
questions.explanation: The CMCS is focused on monitoring aircraft systems for faults, processing fault information, and supplying maintenance messages; general flight operations information (planning/performance tools) is instead provided through the OIS flight operations domain, not the CMC.

questions.question: Before the FMS can start navigating, what must the crew confirm to the system?
options: A. The cabin communication system status
questions.explanation: The FMS derives a start position from the selected flight plan and presents it as the present position; the crew must confirm this present position before the FMS begins to navigate.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a required input to TCAS II?
options: A. Radio altitude and pressure altitude
C. Own aircraft's maximum cruising true airspeed capability
questions.explanation: TCAS II's required inputs are the aircraft address code, air-to-air Mode S transmissions, own aircraft's maximum cruising true airspeed, pressure altitude, and radio altitude — a GPS-derived coordinate is not among these listed inputs.
